title: Scheme presentation from invariant affine free-action charts
statement: Let M be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let G be a finite abstract group acting on M by scheme automorphisms. Suppose the action relation (g,m) maps to (gm,m) monomorphically into M times M [def-pc-fibre-product], with relation scheme the coproduct of G copies of M. Suppose every point x has an affine open neighborhood U [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] such that a(g) inverse-image U = U for every g. Then there exist a scheme Q and a morphism q:M to Q which is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and the square with top map (g,m) to gm, left map (g,m) to m, and other two maps q is a pullback. No separatedness, Noetherianity, finite type, or invertibility of the order of G is assumed.

proof.text: Form the action groupoid on R = coproduct_G M. The source is the fold, the target is the action on each summand, the unit is the 1-summand, inverse sends (g,m) to (g inverse,gm), and composition multiplies the labels. The group laws prove the groupoid identities. Source and target are etale, by the source-local property and their isomorphism restrictions to the summands. They are surjective using the unit. Freeness is the assumed monomorphism, so this is an etale equivalence relation on every test scheme, including disconnected schemes with locally constant labels.

proof.text: Apply the etale relation presentation theorem to its fppf quotient sheaf F. It gives an etale surjection h_M to F, the specified relation as the kernel pair, and etale-local lifts of all sections to M.

proof.text: For every invariant affine open U=Spec A from the hypothesis, the restricted relation is coproduct_G U. This is Spec of the finite product of copies of A. The fold is finite free on the coordinate idempotents, and the target differs from it by a summandwise automorphism. Thus both maps are finite locally free, and freeness restricts. Apply the affine finite locally free relation quotient theorem to get an affine quotient Q_U with the restricted relation as its kernel pair.

source.place: Tag 07S6 (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence-global), finite constant free-action case; Tag 0BBM (lemma-quotient-separated), (4). The finite etale torsor and geometric orbit clauses are the constant-group specialization of the relation identity in 07S6.

proof.text: The finding-opens theorem identifies h_(Q_U) to F with an open subfunctor. For a map h_T to F, choose an etale cover of T with lifts into M. The preimages of the given invariant affine opens cover each lift, so the open subfunctors Q_U cover T by surjectivity of that cover. Since an fppf sheaf is a Zariski sheaf, the scheme representability criterion glues these open charts to Q. Transport the atlas and its kernel-pair square through the representation. This gives exactly the asserted etale surjection and prescribed pullback. For empty M use the empty open cover and the empty scheme.

theorem exists_admissible_free_finite_quotient_presentation
    (M : Scheme.{u}) (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (a : G →* Aut M)
    [Mono (prod.lift (Sigma.desc (fun g : G ↦ (a g).hom))
      (Sigma.desc (fun _ : G ↦ 𝟙 M)))]
    (hcover : ∀ x : M, ∃ U : M.affineOpens,
      x ∈ U.1 ∧ ∀ g : G, (a g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1 = U.1) :
    ∃ (Q : Scheme.{u}) (q : M ⟶ Q), Etale q ∧ Surjective q ∧
      IsPullback (Sigma.desc (fun g : G ↦ (a g).hom))
        (Sigma.desc (fun _ : G ↦ 𝟙 M)) q q
